title: Cryptography
description: Flaws in cryptographic algorithm selection, key generation, entropy sources, padding schemes, and protocol handshakes.

attacks.name: Weak TLS config
attacks.desc: Deploying web servers supporting outdated TLS versions (TLS 1.0/1.1) or weak cipher suites with small key sizes susceptible to decryption and man-in-the-middle attacks.
attacks.prevention: Use current TLS versions and cipher suites from maintained server profiles, and rescan after configuration changes.

attacks.name: SSL stripping / HSTS bypass
attacks.desc: Intercepting initial unencrypted HTTP requests and stripping HTTPS redirects to force communications over plaintext HTTP when HSTS preloading is not configured.
attacks.prevention: Redirect to HTTPS, deploy HSTS only after the site is ready, and avoid sending sensitive content over HTTP.

attacks.name: Weak password hashing
attacks.desc: Storing user passwords using obsolete cryptographic digests (MD5, SHA-1, single-round SHA-256) susceptible to high-speed GPU cracking and rainbow table lookups.
attacks.prevention: Hash passwords with a modern password KDF such as Argon2id, with an appropriate work factor and unique salts.

attacks.name: Unsalted password hashes
attacks.desc: Failing to apply unique cryptographic salts per user before hashing passwords, allowing attackers to identify identical passwords across users and utilize precomputed tables.
attacks.prevention: Use a unique cryptographically random salt for every password before hashing with a suitable password KDF.

attacks.name: ECB mode detection
attacks.desc: Using Electronic Codebook (ECB) cipher mode where identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks, preserving visual and structural patterns in encrypted data.
attacks.prevention: Use authenticated encryption modes such as AES-GCM rather than ECB, and protect keys and nonces.

attacks.name: Padding oracle
attacks.desc: Exploiting differences in server error responses regarding PKCS#7 cryptographic padding validity to decrypt ciphertexts or forge ciphertexts byte-by-byte without the key.
attacks.prevention: Use an authenticated cipher and avoid leaking padding or decryption details through errors or timing.

attacks.name: CBC bit-flipping
attacks.desc: Flipping bits in the initialization vector (IV) or previous ciphertext block in CBC mode to produce predictable 1-to-1 modifications in the decrypted plaintext.

attacks.name: IV reuse
attacks.desc: Reusing Initialization Vectors with the same key in stream ciphers or modes like CTR and GCM, destroying confidentiality and allowing algebraic plaintext recovery.

attacks.name: Weak PRNG for tokens
attacks.desc: Generating session IDs, reset tokens, or cryptographic keys using non-cryptographic pseudo-random number generators (e.g. Math.random(), rand()) with low entropy.

attacks.name: Predictable token seeding
attacks.desc: Seeding random number generators with predictable system timestamps or PID values, allowing attackers to replay the generator sequence and predict future tokens.

attacks.name: Hardcoded keys / secrets
attacks.desc: Embedding static encryption keys, HMAC secrets, or private keys directly in source code, client binaries, or configuration repositories.

attacks.name: Key leakage in JS bundle
attacks.desc: Accidentally bundling private backend API keys, cloud master keys, or signing secrets into publicly accessible front-end JavaScript bundles.

attacks.name: Certificate validation bypass
attacks.desc: Disabling TLS certificate trust verification (e.g. verify=False, rejectUnauthorized: false) in backend HTTP clients, enabling trivial man-in-the-middle attacks.

attacks.name: Encrypted cookie tampering
attacks.desc: Tampering with encrypted cookies when encryption is performed without cryptographic authentication (MAC/AEAD), allowing malleability attacks.

attacks.name: Crypto downgrade
attacks.desc: Tampering with cryptographic protocol negotiations to coerce communicating systems into falling back to legacy, breakable encryption algorithms.

attacks.name: Nonce reuse
attacks.desc: Reusing a cryptographic 'number used once' in authentication protocols or authenticated encryption, leading to message replay or secret key recovery.

attacks.name: Length extension attack
attacks.desc: Exploiting hash algorithms like MD5 and SHA-1/SHA-256 where an attacker knowing Hash(secret || message) and message length can calculate Hash(secret || message || padding || extension) without knowing the secret.
